section_summary: This section concerns Japanese government, municipal, and corporate bonds held outside Japan after the war. The State Department explains its limited role to individual holders, forwards bond data to occupation authorities, and considers requests from Swiss holders. It also includes records on Japanese mission funds in Vatican City, yen deposits, corporate share custody, and a proposed Japanese rehabilitation budget.

subfiles.title: Fragment of bondholder letter
subfiles.about: A closing fragment of an August 13 letter survives.
subfiles.summary: Only a name fragment and date appear.

subfiles.title: Reply to Helen R. P. Green on Japanese government bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains the Department's policy toward her Imperial Japanese Government dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: The August 1 release concerned equity, not bonds. The Department suggests contacting the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and submitting bond and citizenship details; future treaty treatment remains unknown.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese dollar bond data to Tokyo
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards Foreign Bondholders Protective Council information for possible protection of American bond interests.
subfiles.summary: Transmits bond data and the Council's 1941–1944 report to occupation authorities.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from Foreign Bondholders Protective Council letter
subfiles.about: Estimates corporate Japanese dollar bonds held outside Japan.
subfiles.summary: Wylie estimates $43,534,500 across ten corporate issues was held outside Japan and identifies Japanese trustees.

subfiles.title: Trustees for dollar loans
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese trustees and fiscal agency terms for dollar bond issues.
subfiles.summary: Names Mitsui, Industrial Bank of Japan, and Yokohama Specie Bank trustee roles.

subfiles.title: Fiscal agents for dollar loans
subfiles.about: Compares outstanding Japanese bonds with estimated holdings outside Japan by fiscal agent.
subfiles.summary: Totals $283,397,200 outstanding and $88,825,700 presumably held outside Japan.

subfiles.title: Statement of Japanese dollar loans
subfiles.about: Lists issuance, maturity, and outstanding amounts for fourteen Japanese dollar bond issues.
subfiles.summary: Records fourteen issues with $468,130,000 originally issued and $283,397,000 outstanding.

subfiles.title: Wylie letter to Frederick Livesey
subfiles.about: Sends memoranda on Japanese dollar bond holdings and possible sources of further data.
subfiles.summary: Estimates $43,534,500 in ten corporate bond issues outside Japan and suggests Treasury TFR-500 reports.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese trustees and successor fiscal agents
subfiles.about: Urges successor trustees and a successor fiscal agent for Japanese dollar loans.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum identifies Japanese bank trustees for corporate issues and the liquidating Yokohama Specie Bank agency for government-backed issues. It proposes replacement appointments to protect bondholders.

subfiles.title: Fiscal agents for dollar loans, enclosed copy
subfiles.about: Tabulates outstanding dollar bonds and estimated holdings outside Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lists fiscal agents and an estimated $88,825,700 held outside Japan.

subfiles.title: Statement of Japanese dollar loans, enclosed copy
subfiles.about: Details fourteen bond issues, holders, trustees, and fiscal agents.
subfiles.summary: The table compares reported holdings in Japan and outside Japan and identifies fiscal agents and trustees for each issue.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mutsu Ryugo on Japanese bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains policy on her government and Tokyo Electric Light bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department distinguishes bonds from the equity interests covered by its August release, refers Ryugo to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and requests holding and citizenship details.

subfiles.title: Mutsu Ryugo statement of bond holdings
subfiles.about: Reports Imperial Japanese Government and Tokyo Electric Light bonds.
subfiles.summary: Lists her bond holdings and identifying numbers.

subfiles.title: Helen K. Reith bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Reports a Tokyo Electric Light bond after reading a clipping.
subfiles.summary: Identifies her Tokyo Electric Light dollar bond and purchase date.

subfiles.title: Reply to Helen K. Reith
subfiles.from: James W. Gantenbein, Department of State
subfiles.about: Clarifies that the August release did not request Tokyo Electric Light bond data.
subfiles.summary: The release sought unreported equity interests affected by monopoly dissolution.

subfiles.title: National City Bank inquiry about Japanese debts
subfiles.from: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Asks whether ordinary commercial debts fall under the August 1 notice.
subfiles.summary: The bank holds notes and drafts from Japanese borrowers and asks whether to register them.

subfiles.title: Reply to National City Bank
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.to: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Clarifies that the release applied to equity rather than debtor-creditor claims.
subfiles.summary: The Department expects ordinary debt holders to use usual enforcement methods when practicable.

subfiles.title: Reply to Bank of Montreal
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Responds to the bank's report of Tokyo Electric Light bonds held for British clients.
subfiles.summary: The August release was directed to American equity holders. The Department suggests contacting the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, whose settlements may cover all holders of an issue.

subfiles.title: Bank of Montreal report of bonds in custody
subfiles.about: Reports $3,000 in Tokyo Electric Light bonds held for J. & A. Scrimgeour.
subfiles.summary: Identifies British clients and their bonds for possible protection during monopoly dissolution.

subfiles.title: Hammack & Hammack inquiry on franc bonds
subfiles.about: Asks how to collect on Japanese bonds previously discussed with the Department.
subfiles.summary: Requests a collection procedure or a more suitable agency to contact.

subfiles.title: Reply to Hammack & Hammack
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Advises counsel for Elizabeth J. McCloy about Japanese government franc bonds.
subfiles.summary: Reiterates the suggestion to contact American and French bondholder councils.

subfiles.title: Swiss Legation request to register Japanese securities
subfiles.about: Asks whether Swiss nationals may register Japanese corporate securities for protection.
subfiles.summary: Lists major bond issues in Swiss hands and notes discussion with Henry D. Owens.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Swiss Legation
subfiles.about: Offers to forward Swiss holding information to occupation authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Department will transmit submissions to SCAP but cannot promise protection before Allied policy is settled.

subfiles.title: Gowen telegram on Japanese mission funds
subfiles.about: Reports transfer of former Japanese diplomatic mission funds into an Allied trust account.
subfiles.summary: Funds were placed in a Vatican City bank with Allied approval.

subfiles.title: Hammack & Hammack acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Acknowledges advice and sends a copy of counsel's letter to the bondholders council.
subfiles.summary: Reports that counsel contacted the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.title: Hammack & Hammack letter to bondholders council
subfiles.about: Seeks representation for Elizabeth J. McCloy's unpaid Japanese franc bonds.
subfiles.summary: Describes 31 bonds and unpaid coupons and asks about protective action and a French council.

subfiles.title: Despatch on Allied joint trust account
subfiles.about: Reports control of former Japanese diplomatic mission funds at the Holy See.
subfiles.summary: An Allied trust account holds lire 1,449,692.90; two letters are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Bank confirmation of Allied trust account
subfiles.from: Alberto Diorio, Istituto per le Opere di Religione
subfiles.to: Office of the Personal Representative of the President to the Pope
subfiles.about: Confirms the joint account and monthly allowance for Masahide Kanayama.
subfiles.summary: The bank confirms joint control, a 50,000-lire monthly allowance, and written approval for extra expenses.

subfiles.title: Instructions for Allied trust account
subfiles.from: D. G. Osborne and Franklin C. Gowen
subfiles.to: Istituto per le Opere di Religione
subfiles.about: Sets joint control and authorized payments from former Japanese mission funds.
subfiles.summary: The signatories authorize Kanayama's living allowance, require written approval for other expenses, and direct return of the balance after his family's departure.

subfiles.title: Reply to T. C. Young
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains policy concerning three Tokyo Electric Light bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department records Young's holdings, suggests the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and describes data sent to SCAP. It cannot predict peace treaty treatment or priority among claims.

subfiles.title: T. C. Young bondholder letter
subfiles.about: Asks how to recover payment on three Tokyo Electric Light bonds.
subfiles.summary: Young reports no wartime interest and says he needs the money for living expenses.

subfiles.title: Reply to Tsuyoshi Nakahara
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains prospects for Yokohama and Tokyo Electric Light bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes private enforcement, possible council assistance, and data supplied to SCAP. It requests bond and citizenship details and says future treaty treatment is uncertain.

subfiles.title: Tsuyoshi Nakahara bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks about value, unpaid interest, frozen funds, and claim procedures for Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Nakahara names Tokyo Electric Light, Yokohama, and Japanese government bonds. He asks whether frozen bank funds can cover overdue interest and what bondholders should file.

subfiles.title: Transmission of International Standard Electric request
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards a request to verify securities held for International Standard Electric.
subfiles.summary: Requests feasible action on certificates of securities in Japanese custody.

subfiles.title: Reply to H. C. Roemer
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports forwarding his securities verification request to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Promises to forward any response to Arthur Andersen & Co.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum for International Standard Electric letter
subfiles.about: Routes the corporation's December 23 letter for action.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the attached letter to FN.

subfiles.title: International Standard Electric custody request
subfiles.about: Requests certificates confirming Japanese custody of corporate shares for an audit.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Nippon Electric and Sumitomo Electric shares believed held in Japan and asks that certificates go to Arthur Andersen & Co.

subfiles.title: Japanese American Citizens League yen deposit inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks about claims on Japanese yen deposit certificates held by U.S. residents.
subfiles.summary: Raises Fukue Iida's Yokohama Specie Bank certificate and asks whether ownership can be declared.

subfiles.title: Reply on yen deposit certificates
subfiles.about: Explains the absence of a claims process and restrictions on yen balances.
subfiles.summary: No claims procedure or currency conversion is available. Deposits held by persons outside Japan are blocked, while U.S. citizens' property is subject to preservation instructions; the Department offers to inquire about identified accounts.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japanese rehabilitation budget memorandum
subfiles.about: Forwards a recovered budget memorandum with a comparison to Germany funding.
subfiles.summary: Notes the memorandum's delayed arrival and Western Germany's ERP allocation.

subfiles.title: Army rehabilitation request for Japan
subfiles.about: Assesses a $180 million rehabilitation request for occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: Army and SCAP project $452 million in rehabilitation needs for April 1948–June 1949, separate from relief imports. OE supports the request in principle but questions later forecasts and their assumptions.

subfiles.title: Reply to Lillian Pulley
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains policy on her Oriental Development dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department suggests the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, describes its bond statement sent to Tokyo, and requests purchase, payment, and citizenship details. Treaty treatment remains uncertain.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum for Pulley letter
subfiles.about: Forwards Lillian Pulley's inquiry for action.
subfiles.summary: Routes the attached January 12 letter.

subfiles.title: Lillian Pulley bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Lists Oriental Development bonds and asks what action to take.
subfiles.summary: Describes four gold debenture bonds with 1953 and 1958 maturities.

subfiles.title: Swiss Legation transmittal of securities declarations
subfiles.about: Submits 63 bank declarations and asks about registration of government and municipal securities.
subfiles.summary: The Legation supplies declarations of Japanese corporate securities held through Swiss banks and asks whether government and local government bonds may also be declared.

subfiles.title: Bonhôte & Cie declaration
subfiles.about: Certifies a Swiss holding in a Japanese dollar bond.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a Daido bond held by a Swiss citizen.

subfiles.title: Pictet & Cie declaration
subfiles.about: Certifies Gabrielle Chauvet-Ader's Oriental Development bonds.
subfiles.summary: Reports $1,000 in bonds held in New York.

subfiles.title: Bonhôte & Cie Japanese government bond declaration
subfiles.about: Certifies a Swiss citizen's Imperial Japanese Government bond.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a $500 bond from the 1924–1954 issue.

subfiles.title: Banque Union de Crédit declaration
subfiles.about: Reports Oriental Development bonds owned by Swiss nationals.
subfiles.summary: Lists $10,000 in 1953 bonds.

subfiles.title: Gonet & Co. declaration
subfiles.about: Reports bonds owned by a Swiss company and deposited in England.
subfiles.summary: Identifies $2,000 in Oriental Development bonds.

subfiles.title: Crédit Suisse Neuchâtel declaration
subfiles.about: Reports a Taiwan Electric Power bond held for Swiss nationals.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a $1,000 bond due in 1971.

subfiles.title: Banque de l'État de Fribourg declaration
subfiles.about: Reports an Oriental Development bond owned by an American company.
subfiles.summary: Identifies one $1,000 bond due in 1953.

subfiles.title: Roguin & Cie declaration
subfiles.about: Certifies Swiss ownership of a Great Consolidated Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a $1,000 Series A bond.

subfiles.title: Union Bank of Switzerland Winterthur declaration
subfiles.about: Lists Tokyo Electric Light bonds held for a Swiss client.
subfiles.summary: Reports two $1,000 mortgage bonds due in 1953.

subfiles.title: Crédit Suisse Lausanne declaration
subfiles.to: Swiss Legation via Swiss Bankers Association
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese dollar bonds belonging to Swiss holders.
subfiles.summary: Lists $2,000 each in Oriental Development and Taiwan Electric Power bonds.

subfiles.title: Crédit Suisse Glarus declaration
subfiles.about: Certifies a Swiss citizen's Oriental Development bond.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a $1,000 bond and its coupon status.

subfiles.title: Crédit Suisse Geneva declaration
subfiles.about: Reports a Great Consolidated Electric Power bond for Swiss holders.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a $1,000 bond from the 1944 issue.

subfiles.title: Crédit Suisse Bern declaration
subfiles.about: A badly damaged declaration appears to list Japanese bond holdings.
subfiles.summary: Bond details are largely illegible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Crédit Suisse Basel declaration on Great Consolidated bond
subfiles.about: Certifies Swiss ownership of a Great Consolidated Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a $1,000 bond and requests protection of Swiss interests.

subfiles.title: Crédit Suisse Basel declaration on Oriental Development and Tokyo Electric Light bonds
subfiles.about: Certifies Swiss ownership of bonds held locally or in New York.
subfiles.summary: Lists $2,000 in Oriental Development and $1,000 in Tokyo Electric Light bonds.

subfiles.title: Crédit Suisse Zurich list of Japanese dollar bonds
subfiles.about: Lists Swiss-owned bonds of four Japanese issuers.
subfiles.summary: Reports Great Consolidated, Oriental Development, Taiwan Electric Power, and Tokyo Electric Light holdings.

subfiles.title: Lugano declaration on Taiwan Electric Power bond
subfiles.about: Certifies Swiss ownership of a Taiwan Electric Power bond in New York custody.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a $1,000 bond held at Guaranty Trust Company.

subfiles.title: Union Bank of Switzerland Lausanne securities list
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese corporate dollar bonds held in its vaults for Swiss owners.
subfiles.summary: Names Oriental Development, Tokyo Electric Light, Great Consolidated, and Taiwan Electric Power issues.

subfiles.title: Union Bank of Switzerland Geneva non-Swiss holdings declaration
subfiles.about: Reports Oriental Development bonds held for Italian and German interests.
subfiles.summary: Lists three groups of bonds whose beneficial owners have Italian or German connections.
